# Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/d7419c16-e25d-4a6e-b9ec-d72c4bbf1d74)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

For an integer grid named `matrix`, determine the maximum number of cells in any strictly increasing route. A route may begin and finish at arbitrary cells, and each step can go only to the neighboring cell above, below, left, or right. Every next value on the route must be greater than the preceding value.

### Input/Output Requirements
- Input: `matrix`, a two-dimensional integer array whose dimensions are each in the range [0, 200].
- Output: Return an integer equal to the greatest possible increasing-route length.

### Example Input
```plaintext
[
  [7, 8, 5],
  [6, 3, 4],
  [1, 2, 9]
]
```

This is the longest increasing path in the grid.","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"matrix","label":"Matrix","values":["[7, 8, 5]","[6, 3, 4]","[1, 2, 9]"],"marks":{"found":[]}}]}],"expected":"6"}



### Example Output
```plaintext
6
```

The route $$1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 5 \to 8$$ has six cells, so the result is `6`.

### Example
```text
Input: [[3,4],[2,1]]
Output: 4
```

The sequence $$1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4$$ is a valid increasing route with length `4`.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of this as a directed graph where edges go from smaller to larger neighboring values, you're looking for the longest path.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Dynamic programming with memoization (DFS + cache) is the standard approach, computing the longest increasing path starting from each cell.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity target is O(n * m) for an n×m matrix, as each cell's result is computed once.

</details>
